罗大夫回到了她的办公室，手里端着搪瓷缸子，一动不动地坐在椅子上。

缸子里的茶早就凉了，她也没喝。

她从一九六八年被调入这个卫生院，见过的年轻医生多了。北医来的、协和来的、部队来的，谁不是带着一肚子理论知识，信心满满地下乡，最后被现实碰得头破血流？有的连个感冒发烧都看不好，有的打个针能把病人打晕，有的开了一堆药，病人吃了拉肚子。理论一套一套的，动起手来就不是那么回事了。

可眼前这个年轻人的手法，远不止学过正骨这么简单。

她闭上眼睛，在脑子里把王建新的手法过了一遍。他的推拿手法里，有北派正骨的刚猛——那一下旋按，力道足，位置准，没有几年功夫下不来。又有南派伤科的细腻——指腹在筋结上的揉按，轻重缓急，恰到好处。甚至还有她只在祖辈口述中听说过的“意”“气”“合”“一”的境界。

她能看出这手法至少有几种流派的融合。但那种以意引气、以气御力的功夫，连她也只在祖父口中听说过，七十年了，从未亲眼见过。

她睁开眼，端起搪瓷缸子，抿了一口凉茶。茶苦，涩，跟她的心情一样。

这时候，刘晓东凑到王建新身边，压低了声音：“队长，罗大夫刚才在门口站了好一会儿。”

王建新没抬头，继续写病历，笔尖在纸上沙沙地响。

“知道了。”

赵德明院长站在走廊另一头，把这一切看在眼里。他搓了搓手，脸上的笑容深了几分，回头对身边的一个年轻医生说：“去，把住院部的空床位清一清，弄干净点，铺上新床单。”

年轻医生应了一声，转身跑了。

上午九点半，卫生院骨科诊室门口停了一辆平板车。

车上躺着一个四十多岁的男人，右臂上夹着两块木板，用布条胡乱绑着，布条勒得紧，勒出了一道道红印子。整条胳膊肿得发紫，从肩膀一直肿到手指头，皮肤绷得发亮。手腕处扭曲成一个不自然的角度，看着就疼。

“罗大夫，我男人从房上摔下来了。”女人站在车边，眼泪止不住地流，“县医院说要开刀，得花好多钱。我们哪拿得出那么多钱啊？罗大夫，您给想想办法吧……”

罗大夫走过去，弯腰看了看病人的胳膊。她没说话，让人把病人抬到检查床上，然后拆掉木板。木板一拿开，病人的胳膊晃了一下，他咬紧了牙，额头上青筋暴起，但一声没吭。

罗大夫的手指沿着肿胀的臂骨轻轻滑动，从肩膀到手腕，一寸一寸地摸。她的眼睛半闭着，像是睡着了，但手指上的触觉比眼睛还准。

“桡骨远端粉碎性骨折。尺骨茎突撕脱。”她嘴里念叨着，眉头都没皱一下。

她把手洗干净，然后开始了。

先拔伸牵引。她一只手握住病人的手腕，一只手按住他的肘部，慢慢用力，将错位的骨断端拉开。病人的胳膊在她手里像一根柔软的藤条，她使的是巧劲，不是蛮力。骨头被拉开了，她再用端挤提按，将粉碎的骨块一块一块地复位。碎骨头在她手指间滑动，咔嗒咔嗒地响，每一下都回到该回的位置。

最后是那手独门绝技——摸、接、端、提、按、摩、推拿，一气呵成。

不到五分钟。

病人疼得满头大汗，汗水顺着脸颊往下淌，把枕头都打湿了。但他咬着一块毛巾，一声没吭。他老婆在旁边看着，心疼得直跺脚，但不敢出声。

罗大夫让人去院里找来两块杨木板，用锯子锯成合适的长度和弧度，拿砂纸打磨光滑了，用棉垫衬好，将病人手臂固定好。然后用绷带缠好，缠了一圈又一圈，不紧不松，打了个活结。

Doctor Luo returned to her office, holding the enamel jar in his hand and sitting motionless on the chair.

The tea in the jar had long since gone cold, and she didn't drink it.

She was transferred to this health center in 1968 and has met many young doctors.Who came from Peking University, Peking Union Medical College, or the military? Who didn’t go to the countryside with a lot of theoretical knowledge and full of confidence, only to be beaten to death by reality?Some can't even treat a cold or fever, some can knock the patient out with an injection, and some prescribe a bunch of medicine and the patient has diarrhea.The theory is one set, but when it comes to practice, it's not the same thing.

But the technique of the young man in front of me goes far beyond just learning how to set bones.

She closed her eyes and went through Wang Jianxin's techniques in her mind.His massage technique has the fierceness of the Northern School of bone-setting - that single twisting massage is powerful and accurate, and it won't take a few years to get it right.There is also the delicacy of the southern trauma department - the rubbing of the fingertips on the tendons, the priority is just right.There was even a realm of "meaning", "qi", "unity" and "oneness" that she had only heard about from the oral accounts of her ancestors.

She could tell that the technique was a fusion of at least several schools.But she had only heard about the skill of using the mind to guide Qi and using Qi to control force, but she had never seen it with her own eyes in seventy years.

She opened her eyes, picked up the enamel jar, and took a sip of herbal tea.The tea was bitter and astringent, just like her mood.

At this time, Liu Xiaodong approached Wang Jianxin and lowered his voice: "Captain, Doctor Luo was standing at the door for a long time."

Wang Jianxin did not raise his head and continued to write the medical record, the pen tip rustling on the paper.

"Got it."

Dean Zhao Deming stood at the other end of the corridor and saw all this.He rubbed his hands, the smile on his face deepened a little, and turned back to a young doctor beside him and said: "Go, clear out the empty beds in the inpatient department, make them clean, and put down new sheets."

The young doctor responded, turned around and ran away.

At 9:30 in the morning, a flatbed truck stopped at the door of the orthopedic clinic of the health center.

Lying in the car was a man in his forties, holding two wooden boards in his right arm, tied haphazardly with strips of cloth. The strips were tightened so tightly that they left red marks.The entire arm was swollen purple, from the shoulder to the fingers, and the skin was stretched and shiny.The wrist is twisted into an unnatural angle and it hurts to look at it.

"Doctor Luo, my man fell off the house." The woman stood by the car, tears streaming down her face. "The county hospital said it would cost a lot of money to perform an operation. How can we get so much money? Doctor Luo, please think of a way..."

Doctor Luo walked over and bent down to look at the patient's arm.She didn't say anything, and had people lift the patient to the examination bed, and then remove the wooden board.As soon as the board was removed, the patient's arm swayed. He gritted his teeth and veins popped out on his forehead, but he didn't say a word.

Dr. Luo's fingers gently slid along the swollen arm bones, touching inch by inch from the shoulder to the wrist.Her eyes were half closed, as if she was asleep, but the touch on her fingers was more accurate than her eyes.

"Comminuted fracture of the distal radius. Avulsion of the ulnar styloid process." She muttered without even frowning.

She washed her hands and started.

First pull and stretch.She held the patient's wrist with one hand and pressed his elbow with the other, and slowly used force to pull the dislocated bone fragments apart.The patient's arm was like a soft rattan in her hand. She used skillful strength, not brute force.The bones were pulled apart, and she used end-to-end squeezing, lifting and pressing to reset the shattered bones piece by piece.The broken bones slid between her fingers, making a clicking sound, returning to their rightful place every time.

Finally, there are the unique skills of that hand - touching, receiving, lifting, lifting, pressing, massaging, and massaging, all in one go.

Less than five minutes.

The patient was sweating profusely from the pain, and the sweat dripped down his face and wet the pillow.But he bit a towel and said nothing.His wife was watching from the side, stamping her feet in distress, but did not dare to make a sound.

Doctor Luo asked people to go to the hospital to find two poplar boards, cut them into appropriate lengths and arcs with a saw, polished them smooth with sandpaper, lined them with cotton pads, and fixed the patient's arms.Then wrap it with a bandage, wrap it around and around, not tight but not loose, and tie it into a slip knot.
